p: Southampton has been a gateway to the world for centuries. The Mayflower set out from here before stopping at Plymouth, and the Titanic sailed from the city's docks in 1912. Today it's one of the UK's busiest cruise ports, so there's often a steady stream of visitors arriving and leaving, all looking for something fun to do.

Southampton Central station is a short walk from the city centre, with fast trains from London Waterloo and along the south coast. If you're driving, the M3 and M27 bring you close to the city, and there are plenty of car parks. The city centre is easy to walk around, with the shops of Westquay at its heart.

For a group outing, book early, especially if there's a big match at St Mary's or a cruise ship in. Plan your teams, decide on a few prizes, and make sure everyone knows when to arrive. Games bars are a great way to kick off a celebration, and they keep everyone together before the night moves on.

With extra time, Southampton has plenty to explore. Tudor House and Garden is one of the oldest buildings in the city, telling the story of 800 years of Southampton life. The Solent Sky museum is dedicated to aviation history, including the Spitfire, which was designed in the city. And the ferries to the Isle of Wight run from the docks, making a day trip across the Solent easy. The New Forest, with its ponies and pretty villages, is just a short drive west.
